paragraphs.text: A [Liu An basket tea](liu-an:definition) from 1990, the [dark tea](dark:definition) made in Qimen County in southern Anhui from the local Qimen bush that Keemun red tea also comes from, not in Lu'an as the name suggests. This lot was packed into small bamboo baskets lined with [bamboo leaf](liu-an:basket), and it was never piled to ferment: its change has been slow and natural, left to the years.

The tea was made for the [southern trade](liu-an:southern-trade), drunk in Guangdong, Hong Kong, Macau and among the overseas Chinese of Southeast Asia, and kept in homes and medicine shops. War stopped production in the 1930s and 1940s. In 1983 tea people from Hong Kong sent an aged basket to Anhui and asked for it to be made again, and commercial making returned in the early 1990s. This basket dates from 1990. At thirty-six years it has had a long time in the basket, which is where [Liu An is said to improve](liu-an:ageing).

brewing.text: Use water at or near the boil, rinse the leaf quickly, and keep the steeps short, each a little longer than the last, in a gaiwan or clay pot; doses run from about 3 to 8 grams for 100 ml, for six to ten or more steeps. A small piece of the basket's bamboo leaf is often brewed with it. Aged tea can also be simmered in a larger pot, about 1 gram to 200 to 300 ml, for a few minutes or longer.

notice.text: A redder, browner liquor, the smoke gone, and the cup moving toward medicinal, woody and camphor notes, often with betel nut.
